title: The 32 bits as hex
starter: let hex32 (x : int) : string = Printf.sprintf "%08x" x
hints: Try the starter on `-1`. OCaml's `int` has 63 bits, so a negative number has far more than 32 bits set, and `%x` prints all of them.
Keep only the low 32 bits before printing: `x land 0xFFFFFFFF` is a count from 0 to 2^32 - 1, whatever `x` was.
explain: `x land 0xFFFFFFFF` keeps the low 32 bits as a non-negative `int`, which is the plain-count reading of the wheel. `%08x` prints it as hex, padded to 8 digits. -1 and 2^32 - 1 have the same low 32 bits, so they print the same, and so do -2147483648 and 2147483648.
